text:
mike-provisioner: noticed repeated OOB link flaps in ap-south1 this morning. BMC keepalive resets every ~5m, VLAN tag appears sticky on the management NIC, and secureboot bit toggles after some reboots. Provisioner is failing GPUs during node bringup -> a bunch of evictions. anyone else seeing this?

deploy-bot: firmware-rollout: starting bmc-fw v1.2.4 -> v1.2.5 to ap-south1 (canary: 5 nodes).

sara-infra: yep seeing the same. PXE fails during first boot intermittently, tftp times out on the oob bridge. queue backlog up ~120 nodes and counting. rolling back isn't straightforward because the images are signed with the new secureboot keys.

james-sre: can we scope to NIC vendor / driver? iirc we had a similar vlan-sticky issue with Mellanox updates in eu1 last year. can you paste the oob logs?

mike-provisioner: here's the last dmesg from the BMC side for a failed boot (node-23):
```
[  102.123456] ipmi_oob: link-state change: down->up
[  102.128900] ipmitool: vlan tag 0x8100 stale on eth0. clearing failed: EIO
[  102.129001] secureboot: nvram flag toggled (1->0) during reboot sequence
[  102.130200] pxe: tftp read timed out after 5s
```

elaine-ops: if secureboot flips during provisioning, we risk marking those nodes untrusted and auto-evicting attached GPUs to avoid tainted workloads. quick calc: to cover the evictions and reprovisioning we might need ~200 spare GPUs across regions -> extra cost estimate ~ $4k/day until stabilized.

sara-infra: short-term workaround: set `oob.keepalive_interval=30s` (was 5s) and clear the sticky VLAN on the BMC via `ipmitool lan set 1 arp 0` then `ipmitool raw 0x30 0x70 0` to force re-sync. i'm running that on node-23 now as a canary.

deploy-bot: canary result: node-23 patched, no link flaps for 15m, secureboot nvram stable. marking canary healthy. will apply to canary group of 20 nodes next.

james-sre: plan: pause full rollout until we confirm no secureboot key flip on older hardware. add gating step to the rollout job to check nvram secureboot flag pre/post update and abort if it changed. also add vendor-specific nic driver check.

mike-provisioner: agreed. also add a manual override flag in the provisioner for Dedicated pools so we don't auto-evict GPUs mid-rollout — we need to avoid cascading capacity loss.

elaine-ops: opening a temporary GPU quota bump for us-west1 and us-east1 so we can absorb the spike. i'll also enable a billing alert threshold at +25% run rate.

oob-bot: incident created: INC-2026-2301. assigned: sara-infra, james-sre, mike-provisioner. priority: High. link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-2301

sara-infra: updating runbook now with the `ipmitool` steps, the nvram check, and rollback instructions. adding a note about vendor NIC failcases and where to find the blacklist. :thumbsup:

mike-provisioner: monitoring the canary group. will hold the full rollout and update the provisioning pipeline tomorrow after a post-mortem. last check-in: 3699999035
